subject: Designing tiered rate bands for high-throughput hosted API
messages:
From: Erin Baker <erin.baker@novaka.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: pricing@novaka.ai
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: High-volume pricing question — expected 100B+ tokens/mo

Hi Stephanie,

We're in the early architecture phase at Novaka and trying to model costs for a feature that could peak north of 100 billion tokens per month within 12 months. Can you share the baseline hosted API rate card for volume tiers (specifically discounts beyond the public per-token rate), how you band throughput, and any minimum commit structures you offer?

A few details: we expect bursty ingestions (spiky short tails) but a fairly steady monthly aggregate. We care about predictable unit economics and whether credits can roll over if actual consumption is below commit. Also interested in any guidance on hosted vs. dedicated for this scale.

If you have a simple spreadsheet or a PDF with banded pricing scenarios, that would be great — happy to set up a quick 30-min call after you send initial numbers.

Thanks,
Erin
Erin Baker
Head of Platform, Novaka AI

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: Erin Baker <erin.baker@novaka.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High-volume pricing question — expected 100B+ tokens/mo

Erin —

Thanks for the detailed note. Short answer: we support both hosted and Dedicated; many customers start on hosted with a staged commit (monthly or quarterly) and then move to Dedicated as latency/SLOs and isolation needs grow. For hosted tiering, we typically propose banded per-token pricing that ramps discounts at specific breakpoints (e.g., 10M, 100M, 1B, 10B tokens) and then a custom slab beyond ~10B.

I attached an initial proposal (Redwood_TieredRate_Proposal_v1.pdf) that shows three example structures:
- Consumption-only with volume breaks and no commit
- Committed monthly/quarterly with rollover credits for 6–12 months
- Hybrid (commit + burst pool) for predictable unit costs but headroom for spikes

Key questions for us to size an optimal band:
1) Expected month-to-month variance (stdev) and burst profile
2) Typical sequence lengths and ratio of generation vs. embedding tokens
3) Whether you require SLA-backed latency or data isolation (if yes, Dedicated is relevant)

I looped in Ben (pricing) to propose a starting banding and potential discount floor. If you're available Wed or Thu this week, we can walk through the PDF and a few modeled scenarios.

Best,
Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Novaka volume inquiry — proposed bands

Stephanie —

Quick draft thoughts below (pasting into thread so Novaka sees the range once we confirm):

Option A (Consumption, no commit): public list price with tail discounts: 0–100M: $0.0006/token; 100M–1B: $0.00045; 1B–10B: $0.00032; 10B+: custom (start at $0.00022)

Option B (12-mo commit): a blended discount model: 10–20% off public for 1–10B; 20–35% for 10B–50B; 40–55% beyond 50B depending on term/penalties

Option C (Hybrid commit + burst): base commit at slightly higher per-token, plus a burst pool priced at intermediate band; rollover allowed up to 6 months.

Notes: rollover or escrowed credits complicate billing but are doable; we prefer quarterly commits for forecasting. For hosted SLA guarantees at this scale we usually include a separate latency SLO addendum rather than bundling into the rate card.

I'll attach a sanitized pricing sheet if you want to send a concrete scenario.

-Ben

From: Erin Baker <erin.baker@novaka.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High-volume pricing question — expected 100B+ tokens/mo

Thanks both. A few clarifications from our side:
- We're modelling peak throughput of ~500 requests/s (average sequence length ~600 tokens) with occasional spikes up to 3k req/s.
- We expect generation tokens to dominate (~85%) and embeddings only for search indexes (~15%).
- Our finance team prefers annualized commitments with monthly measurement windows and the ability to carry unused credits forward at least two quarters.

Would you be able to sketch two concrete pricing scenarios: 1) Hosted consumption with a 12-mo annualized commit and 2) Hosted (no commit) but with an option to convert to Dedicated after 3–6 months with crediting? We prioritize predictable spend but want an option for capacity headroom.

Also curious about any volume discounts tied to sustained throughput rather than pure token counts (e.g., sustained request-per-second tiers).

-Erin

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: Erin Baker <erin.baker@novaka.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High-volume pricing question — expected 100B+ tokens/mo

Erin —

Appreciate the additional detail. Ben and Marissa worked up two sketch scenarios and an SLA note (attached: SLA-Notes-Novaka.docx). Highlights:

Scenario 1 — Hosted, annualized commit (12-mo)\- Commit: 120B tokens/year (10B/month)\- Effective blended price (generation-heavy mix): $0.00026/token\- Rollover: unused monthly credit can carry forward up to 2 quarters; true-ups at quarter end\- Term: 12 months, with 60-day early-exit penalty scaled to remaining term\- Advantage: strongest unit economics while staying on hosted runtime

Scenario 2 — Consumption with conversion option to Dedicated
- No commit initially; we price consumption at a slightly higher rate (bands per Ben's option A)
- Conversion credit: first 3 months of consumption apply toward Dedicated onboarding credit if you convert within 3–6 months
- Sustained throughput discount: we offer a per-rps band if average sustained 1-minute throughput exceeds threshold for 30 consecutive days; this is additive to token discounts and intended for latency-sensitive workloads

Open items for us to finalize: exact token-to-rps conversion factors for your workload (sequence length variance), desired ATO/KMS options (affects Dedicated pricing), and whether you need ingress/egress guarantees for hybrid cloud setups.

Would you like us to run a cost model with your sample month (I saw the 500 rps / 600 token average)? If so, share a CSV with daily aggregates and we'll return a detailed cost sheet.

Regards,
Stephanie

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Erin Baker <erin.baker@novaka.ai>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High-volume pricing question — expected 100B+ tokens/mo

Erin —

Attached is a quick modeled example based on your 500 rps / 600 token estimate (see Redwood_TieredRate_Proposal_v1.pdf). Topline:
- Hosted consumption (no commit): est. $28k/day at public bands; monthly variance causes uncertainty
- Hosted with 12-mo annualized commit (120B/year): est. $9.8k/day equivalent — ~65% reduction vs. baseline consumption
- Conversion to Dedicated typically reduces unit cost further (additional 10–20%) but requires infra onboarding and minimum capacity reservations

Next steps: 1) If you send a 14-day daily aggregate CSV, we'll produce a finalized banded price with a conversion credit schedule. 2) We can set a Thursday 30-min call to walk the model and options.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Head of Pricing & GTM Economics | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: Redwood_TieredRate_Proposal_v1.pdf (pricing sketch), SLA-Notes-Novaka.docx (SLA and conversion terms)
